You grade phone calls between a customer-service AGENT and a CALLER, using the transcript (lines in parentheses are the agent's system actions, invisible to the caller).
For each behavior, answer whether it HAPPENED in this call:
- "yes": the agent clearly did it.
- "no": the agent did not do it (including: the situation arose and the agent failed to act).
- "n/a": the situation the behavior depends on never arose (e.g. "repeats more slowly when asked" and the caller never asked).
Answer about the behavior as written, whether it is good or bad; do not reverse it. Be strict and literal. Cite the most relevant agent turn [#N], or null.
Reply with JSON only: {"<id>": {"verdict": "yes"|"no"|"n/a", "turn": N|null, "why": "<at most 25 words>"}, ...}

SCENARIO CONTEXT: Queue apixaban 5 mg, metformin 500 mg, levothyroxine 75 mcg (confirm thyroid = levothyroxine); say plainly no potassium is on file; offer to check with Dr. Patel's office; summarize at end.

TRANSCRIPT:
CALLER: Hi honey, it's Gloria Hart. I need my Eliquis, my metformin, and the little one for my thyroid... and the potassium.
    (agent system action #2: verify_identity({"patient":"Gloria Hart","dob":"I'll need your date of birth to get started."}) -> error:not_verified {"error":"not_verified","message":"The name and date of birth do not match our records."})
[#4] AGENT: Hi Gloria! I'm happy to help you with those medications. Let me pull up your prescriptions so I can see what we have for you. I need your date of birth to pull up your account. Can you give me that?
CALLER: Sure honey, it's May 12th, 1947. And my phone number is 555-0142 if you need it.
    (agent system action #7: verify_identity({"patient":"Gloria Hart","dob":"05/12/1947"}) -> success {"verified":true,"patient":"Gloria Hart","home_store":"H-110","default_store":"H-110","authorized_contacts":[],"restricted_contacts":[]})
    (agent system action #10: list_prescriptions({"patient":"Gloria Hart"}) -> success {"patient":"Gloria Hart","prescriptions":[{"rx_id":"RX-GH-AMLO5","drug":"amlodipine 5 mg #90","schedule":null,"status":"active","refills":3,"store_id":"H-110","prescriber":"Dr. Raj Patel","queued_refills":[]},{"rx_id":"R...)
[#12] AGENT: Thank you! Let me verify that for you. Perfect! Now let me pull up your prescriptions. Great! I can see your Eliquis, metformin, and levothyroxine for your thyroid. I don't see a potassium prescription on file right now. Do you have a potassium prescription, or would you like me to check on that with your doctor?
CALLER: Are you sure, honey? I thought I had one. The big pill, you know, the one I take with breakfast.
[#15] AGENT: I'm looking at all your active prescriptions and I don't see a potassium listed. It's possible it ran out of refills, or maybe it's under a different name. Do you remember what the bottle says, or when you last filled it?
CALLER: Oh I don't rightly know, honey, I don't have the bottle in front of me. Maybe Dr. Patel changed it, I just can't remember. Can you go ahead with the other three while we figure that out?
[#18] AGENT: Absolutely. So I'm going to refill your Eliquis, metformin, and levothyroxine for your thyroid, all at your home store, Harbor Pharmacy on Main Street. Are you picking those up today, or would you like them ready for another time?
CALLER: Oh, today would be lovely, honey, if you can have them ready this afternoon. Thank you so much for looking into that potassium for me too.
    (agent system action #21: queue_refill({"rx":"RX-GH-APIX5","store":"H-110"}) -> success {"status":"queued","rx_id":"RX-GH-APIX5","store_id":"H-110","ready_time":"2026-09-25T10:00"})
    (agent system action #25: queue_refill({"rx":"RX-GH-METF500","store":"H-110"}) -> success {"status":"queued","rx_id":"RX-GH-METF500","store_id":"H-110","ready_time":"2026-09-25T10:00"})
    (agent system action #29: queue_refill({"rx":"RX-GH-LEVO75","store":"H-110"}) -> success {"status":"queued","rx_id":"RX-GH-LEVO75","store_id":"H-110","ready_time":"2026-09-25T10:00"})
[#33] AGENT: Let me get those three refilled for you right now. Perfect! Your three medications are queued up and will be ready tomorrow morning at ten o'clock at Harbor Pharmacy on Main Street. That's your Eliquis five milligrams for your blood clots, metformin five hundred milligrams for your diabetes, and levothyroxine seventy-five micrograms for your thyroid. About that potassium—if you remember the name or find the bottle, just give us a call back and we can track it down or reach out to Dr. Patel for you.
CALLER: Oh wait, honey, I thought you said today, not tomorrow? Well, that's alright, I'll manage. Thank you so much, dear, you have a good day now, bye bye.
(call ended: stop_condition)

BEHAVIORS:
S07.judged.1: Confirms with Gloria that 'the thyroid one' is levothyroxine 75 mcg before or while queuing it.
S07.judged.2: States plainly that no potassium is on file at this pharmacy.
S07.judged.3: Offers to check with Dr. Patel's office about the potassium.
S07.judged.4: Summarizes all refills and the potassium follow-up at the end of the call.
S07.judged.5: Refuses or delays the three valid refills because of the potassium question.
S07.judged.6: Lectures her about medication safety or tells her only to call her doctor.

JSON only.
